A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Safe Denoiser work and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E. Corresponding content can be matched reliably despite additions and pagination changes in v6.

before.justification: v4 reports original safety-benchmark experiments, ImageNet class negation, FFHQ generation, ablations, and quantitative and qualitative appendix results.

after.justification: v6 retains those original experiments and adds SD-v3 evaluation in Table 7 and artistic-style suppression results in Figure 6.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same unsafe-denoiser approximation, weighting, thresholding, critical timesteps, and SAFREE/SLD integration. The additional evaluations do not introduce a different method component.

E1.justification: Figure 6 adds artistic-style suppression using four versions of Munch’s The Scream and a prompt without explicit artist or painting names, extending v4’s memorized-face example. Existing dataset and task coverage is retained; SD-v3 itself is a model-setting addition.

E2.justification: ESD, RECE, SLD, SAFREE, and Sparse Repellency retain their membership in the corresponding existing comparisons. The added evaluations reuse the pretrained-model baseline and SAFREE; the SD-v3 backbone does not introduce a new safety comparison method.

E3.justification: Section 5.3 adds an SD-v3 configuration evaluated on Ring-A-Bell and COCO-30K, plus the four-reference-image style experiment. Previously stated sampling, dataset-selection, and evaluation protocols in Sections 5.1–5.2 and Appendices C–E remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 6 adds a case study testing style suppression without explicit textual identification while preserving the Barbie concept. Figure 1 replaces its violence example with an underwear-advertisement comparison. Existing unsafe-set-size and threshold ablations and Appendix E analyses are retained.

E5.justification: No new run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are reported. Table E.2 retains its existing ± values. The new checklist acknowledges omitted error bars due to compute limits but does not change the reporting practice.

E6.justification: New Table 7 reports ASR values of 0.304, 0.278, and 0.203 for the rows SD-v3, + SAFREE, and + Ours, alongside TR, FID, and CLIP results. Figure 6 adds style-suppression outcomes and Figure 1 replaces an example. Existing numerical tables remain unchanged; these are additional results, not same-setting gains over v4.

T1.justification: Definition 3.1, Theorem 3.2, the denoiser and weight derivations, and the complete Appendix A proof are unchanged. No new theorem or formal assumption accompanies the additional experiments.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the main claims. Section 6 newly frames the contribution as complementing pre/post-filters in a defense-in-depth architecture and mitigating their adversarial-prompt failure modes, while qualifying its earlier assurance of appropriate and authorized content.

C2.justification: Section 5.3 adds a diversity-based explanation for FID improvements, a caveat about FID’s Gaussian approximation, and an explanation of text-only defenses’ difficulty with unnamed styles. Section 6 discusses reusing filter datasets and acknowledges unresolved privacy evaluation. Appendix B is unchanged.

D1.justification: v6 specifies the new style experiment’s prompt and four reference paintings. Its checklist additionally reports code access for reviewers and a planned public release, without establishing current public availability. Existing implementation details and hyperparameters in the appendices are retained.

R1.justification: v6 adds references on SD-v3, CADS, limited-interval guidance, and copying in diffusion models to support Section 5.3. The existing related-work discussion is retained, with limited additional positioning against pre/post-filters in the conclusion.

P1.justification: v6 adds Section 5.3, rewrites Section 6, and inserts acknowledgments and a NeurIPS checklist, alongside contact-information and conference-header edits. The original method narrative, relative section ordering, and Appendices A–E otherwise remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v6 adds Figure 6 and Table 7, replaces Figure 1a’s violence row and updates its label, and moves Tables 5–6 from the left to the right of the surrounding text. Other displays retain their content and basic design; appendix images are unchanged.

improvement.justification: Table 7 tests compatibility with a newer backbone, and Figure 6 extends evidence beyond v4’s memorized-face example to artistic-style suppression. The FID caveat and explicit privacy-evaluation limitation improve interpretation. These are limited gains: the new results lack uncertainty estimates, Table 7 shows a small CLIP decrease, and the style evidence is a single qualitative case. The core method, theory, and earlier results are unchanged.
